name: RSA Encryption
description: RSA is a public-key cryptosystem widely used for secure data transmission. It enables secure communication over insecure channels without requiring a shared secret key. It's based on the practical difficulty of factoring the product of two large prime numbers.
real_world_examples: Secure messaging apps (Signal, WhatsApp key exchange)
how_it_works: RSA uses two keys: a public key for encryption and a private key for decryption. Key generation involves selecting two large primes p and q, computing n=p*q and φ(n)=(p-1)(q-1), then choosing public exponent e and computing private d such that (d*e) mod φ(n) = 1. Security relies on the difficulty of factoring n.

complexity.time: O(k³) for k-bit keys (using efficient multiplication), O(log e) for encryption, O(log d) for decryption

pseudocode_or_diagram_description: KeyGen: select primes p,q. Compute n=p*q, φ=(p-1)(q-1). Choose e coprime to φ. Compute d=e^-1 mod φ. Public key=(n,e), Private key=(n,d). Encrypt: c = m^e mod n. Decrypt: m = c^d mod n. Fast exponentiation (square-and-multiply) makes this practical.
